summary: ACCEPT. Fixes a live-money exit defect found in production this morning: CW floor mode maintained and PERSISTED a high-water floor but never CONSUMED it, substituting a fixed entry+2% floor. Concretely, live:orb AEHL entered at 6.07, bid peaked 7.58, the generic ratchet stood at ~7.48895, bid fell to 7.46 at 08:49:02 ET -- and the CW branch returned a frozen 6.1914 before that ratchet was ever evaluated. 0 of 376 quote ticks breached 6.1914 (minimum bid 6.20), so nothing sold and the operator closed by hand at +18.6%. ⭐ THE CONTROL WAS ALREADY IN THE SAME LOG: YDDL, same account, same session, same bare-fill extended-hours conditions, breached its fixed -5% stop and exited correctly via CW_HARD_STOP. Downside path worked, upside path did not -- a one-variable contrast that made the diagnosis unambiguous. ⛔ MY OWN HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND CODEX CORRECTED IT: I proposed the profit exit was OCO-gated. It is not -- a missing OCO fails OPEN into the software ladder, and [OMS-OCO-EXIT-MISS] is a separate diagnostic I misread as causal. Their statement of the defect is better than mine and is the one recorded here. ⭐⭐ THE RATIONALE QUESTION WAS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE REVIEW AND CODEX ANSWERED IT BEFORE TOUCHING CODE. I required them to explain why the fixed floor was deliberate before changing it. The helper says it was fixed so it 're-arms identically after an OMS restart -- no durable state needed': chosen for RESTART DETERMINISM, not spread protection. My leading hypothesis (that it guarded against the spread tripping breakeven in 0.5s) was REFUTED as the reason, though the spread hazard remains a live constraint. That answer reshaped the fix: consuming a persisted ratchet reintroduces exactly the durable state the original design avoided, so the whole change is only safe because a lost or stale ratchet DEGRADES TO THE FIXED FLOOR. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED WITH A REAL DENOMINATOR, 07-14 to 08-31: broker-OCO profit exits 339/406 (83.5%), software profit exits 67/406 (16.5%), classification coverage 523/523 with zero COULD_NOT_TELL. The software path HAS run 67 times, so this repairs exercised code rather than shipping untested code. It also explains why the defect hid so long: in RTH the broker bracket silently did the job, and only losing the bracket in extended hours exposed that the software substitutes a FIXED floor for a TRAIL. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION ACROSS TWO ROUNDS. Round 1, baseline 20: M1 (return fixed_floor, regressing to today's bug) DIED. ⛔ M2 (ratchet alone, so a stale-low rehydrated ratchet sinks the floor BELOW entry+2%) SURVIVED. ⛔ M3 (drop the `ratcheted > 0` guard) SURVIVED. ⭐ M3 WAS MY ERROR: it is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT. max(fixed, ratcheted) already returns fixed_floor for zero or negative input, so behaviour was identical and no test could have caught it. I reported it as a coverage gap when the correct answer was 'that guard is redundant'. Codex identified this and REMOVED the branch rather than writing a test for a distinction that does not exist -- the better fix, and a correction to me. Round 2, baseline 21, source delta two lines: M2 replay DIED, killed by test_effective_floor_never_weakens_restart_safe_fixed_floor. ⭐ M4, which I invented after the correction so it cannot have been written to -- min() instead of max(), inverting the invariant -- DIED with 4 failures. M1 replay DIED. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 3e2576bfe8df6dbc. THE SAFETY INVARIANT IS NOW ONE COMPARISON AND IT IS TESTED: max(fixed_floor, ratcheted) means missing, zero, negative or stale-low durable state can never weaken the restart-safe fixed floor; only a strictly higher ratchet wins. That single line is what answers the restart-determinism rationale. BID-ONLY RATCHETING PRESERVED AND CORRECT: an ask spike on a wide spread must not manufacture a ratchet, and codex's bid->ask mutation covers it. NOT MEASURED: I ran the two focused test files, not the full suite -- codex reports 2,954 passed with 14 skipped, taken on report. I did not mutate the _hydrate_v2_position restore path itself, so the persistence half is accepted on code reading plus the degradation invariant above, not on execution. ⛔ DEPLOY: OMS-only restart, AFTER THE CLOSE, and SEPARATE FROM #852 -- do not bundle. Two unexercised changes in one restart destroys attribution, and after this morning each change must be individually attributable.
